headline_answer.question_from_user: 저것을 활용한 논문이 혹시 탑 베뉴에 하나라도 있니? (Is there even one top-venue paper that uses that [injection] approach?)
headline_answer.answer: YES - and the venue-directed search adds three more top-venue instances that the archive sweep could not see, two of them on the user's own named list. The injection ARCHITECTURE is not a preprint curiosity: it is about twenty years of settled practice (this file's own earliest entry is 2008 — see what_the_automotive_line_looks_like: 'Three generations. (1) 2008-2012') in automotive radar simulation and it lives in IEEE TAP, IEEE TMTT, IEEE TAES, IEEE JSAC, and IET RSN (⚠ the IEEE AP-Magazine item is NOT counted — this same file records it as 'NOT OPENED ... content is NOT ESTABLISHED ... do not cite the mechanism until the PDF is in hand', and notes it is a column, not a peer-reviewed Transactions paper). What is NOT in the venue record - after deliberately hunting for it across TAP, TWC, JSAC, TVT, TAES, TMTT, IoT-J, ICASSP, INFOCOM, MobiCom, SenSys, MobiSys, EuCAP, EuRAD and IET RSN - is LAMBDA's exact move: buying a COMMERCIAL full-wave solver's RCS table and multiplying it onto RAY-TRACED propagation paths. Every peer-reviewed instance found sources the table from a measurement campaign or from the authors' OWN asymptotic/ray solver.
headline_answer.the_split_that_matters: The venue record splits on WHO COMPUTES THE TABLE, not on whether tabulating is allowed. Authors' own solver: Schuler TAP 2008, Deep IET RSN 2020 (from archive sweep). Measurement campaign: Abadpour TMTT 2022, Potter TAES 2025, Zhang JSAC 2026 (archive), Zhao SCIS 2025, Das WCL 2026 (archive), Costa J-STEAP 2025 (archive). Commercial full-wave solver into a ray tracer: LAMBDA only, still a preprint; Rzewuski NATO STO 2021 uses a commercial FDTD solver but feeds a link budget, not ray-traced paths.
headline_answer.why_this_is_good_news_for_us: Our outputs/report13_sigma_grid.* is a 9 elevation x 120 azimuth x 3 band table per airframe computed by OUR OWN SBR+PO on Sionna's ray engine. That is the Schuler/Deep flavour - the flavour with an IEEE TAP paper and an IET RSN paper behind it - not the LAMBDA flavour. The architecture is not the thing a reviewer will contest.
headline_answer.the_thing_a_reviewer_will_contest: In every strong-venue instance the tabulated signature is anchored to an independent reference before it is reused: Schuler validates his ray-traced signature against anechoic bistatic measurements at the EC Joint Research Centre before reducing it to clusters, and validates the reduced 10-cluster model back against the full ray-trace; Potter's table IS measurement; Abadpour's IS measurement. The preprint (LAMBDA) does not validate. So the reviewer question is anchoring, not architecture.

quotes.text: The scope of this work is to present a technique to generate a significantly simplified RCS model of the vehicle with a limited number of virtual scattering centers, each with its own scattering characteristic, and how to group these scattering centers in a cluster database. The work is based on ray-tracing simulations of complex vehicle models. The ray-tracing simulations have been validated by measurements.

The position and the amplitude of the scattering centers depend on the radius and the azimuth angle during ray-tracing simulation. This fact has to be taken into account when the derived virtual scattering center model will be used in other radar simulations by calculating the aspect angles for each cluster and the attenuation.

This is important, since only by reducing the complexity of large objects it becomes possible to simulate superior problems like automotive radar scenarios in realistic traffic situations. The herein presented monostatic model offers a proven base for such simulations.

venue_hits_opened.was_the_tabulated_signature_validated: YES, twice. (1) Against measurement: 'The verification measurements were performed in the anechoic chamber of the European Commission Joint Research Center (JRC), located at Ispra in northern Italy' (p.3546), bistatic coupling coefficient, front and rear illumination, both polarizations, 5 degree steps. (2) Against the un-reduced source: the 10-cluster model's monostatic reflection coefficient is compared back to the original full ray-trace, p.3549: 'Considering the first 10 clusters, the agreement between virtual scattering center representation and original ray-tracing simulation is very good for the whole azimuth angle.'
venue_hits_opened.honest_caveat: The paper builds and validates the table; it does not itself run the downstream traffic-scenario simulation that consumes it. Do not cite it as 'injected into a propagation simulator' - cite it as 'computed a reusable aspect-indexed vehicle signature in a ray solver, validated it, and published it in IEEE TAP for exactly that downstream use'.
venue_hits_opened.relevance_to_us: STRONGEST STRUCTURAL PRECEDENT FOUND. Same three steps as ours in the same order: own ray/asymptotic solver -> aspect-indexed signature table -> handoff to a system-level simulator. It is 18 years old and it is in IEEE TAP.

quotes.text: To evaluate the proposed approach, we simulate random walk trajectories for seven drones and correspond the target's aspect angles to Radar Cross Section (RCS) measurements acquired in an anechoic chamber.

This section outlines the process of mapping simulated azimuth and elevation angles to RCS data measured in an anechoic chamber. This involves calculating the target UAV aspect angles (azimuth and elevation) relative to the Radar Line Of Sight (RLOS) while considering the target UAV pose (yaw, pitch, roll and translation).

The azimuth and elevation samples, phi and theta respectively, are mapped to a measured RCS signature sigma in R^F from [38], where we bilinearly interpolate the mapped RCS measurements for continuous azimuth and elevations not collected in [38].

venue_hits_opened.was_the_tabulated_signature_validated: The table IS the measurement, so no separate anchoring step is needed. The paper is explicit that the drones were static during measurement, so the table carries no micro-Doppler and no rotor modulation.
venue_hits_opened.relevance_to_us: This is the closest published analogue of how we USE our grid: an aspect-indexed, multi-frequency sigma table per airframe, interpolated at run time from a simulated trajectory, in a multistatic geometry. IEEE TAES accepted it with a measured table and no propagation channel at all. Our version substitutes a computed table and adds the channel.

the_deliberate_automotive_look.user_hypothesis: 'The automotive-radar simulation literature is the most likely place to find a MATURE version of this ... it may be far better established than in the drone literature.'
the_deliberate_automotive_look.verdict: CONFIRMED, and it is older and more settled than expected. The automotive line is where the vocabulary itself comes from: 'scattering center model', 'cluster database', 'bistatic RCS table look-ups'.
the_deliberate_automotive_look.what_the_automotive_line_looks_like: Three generations. (1) 2008-2012, KIT and TUM/Bosch build the method: Schuler TAP 2008 extracts an aspect-indexed virtual-scattering-center table from a ray solver validated at the EC JRC anechoic chamber; Buddendick and Eibert parameterize the same object with parallelized physical optics and feed it to radio channel simulations (AP-S 2009, VNC 2010, GeMiC 2010, AP-Magazine 2012). (2) 2015-2022, the practice hardens into virtual-validation infrastructure for autonomous driving: measured signature tables (Abadpour TMTT 2022), radar target simulators and over-the-air vehicle-in-the-loop rigs (Buddappagari EuRAD 2021, DOI 10.1109/EuRAD48048.2021.00078), and a survey that treats the precomputed-signature approach as one of the standard model classes (Magosi et al., Sensors 22:5693, 2022, DOI 10.3390/s22155693). (3) 2018-present, the commercial asymptotic solvers absorb the whole pipeline and the handoff disappears - HFSS SBR+, Remcom WaveFarer and Altair Feko run the scenario themselves, which converts the architecture from 'injection' back into 'computed inside the engine'.
the_deliberate_automotive_look.the_uncomfortable_implication_for_us: Generation 3 is why nobody publishes LAMBDA's move at a venue any more in automotive: if you already own an asymptotic ray solver that can do the scenario, you do not export a table and multiply it in. Our position is defensible only because Sionna's stock solver has no scattering integral - i.e. our justification for injecting is a property of OUR engine, not a general claim that injection is the right architecture. Expect a reviewer from the automotive side to make exactly this point.
the_deliberate_automotive_look.quantitative_claim_seen_but_NOT_SOURCED: A search-engine summary of the Magosi survey states 'System simulation complexity has been reduced from approximately 100,000 triangles per vehicle object down to 80 triangles plus additional bistatic RCS table look-ups.' The WebFetch of the survey (PMC9370944) did NOT return that sentence, and it is not in the Schuler PDF (whose model is 12,100 triangles reduced to 10 clusters). TREAT AS UNSOURCED - most likely it belongs to the Buddendick line. Do not quote it.

negative_result_stated_carefully.what_was_hunted: A peer-reviewed venue paper doing LAMBDA's exact move: a COMMERCIAL full-wave EM solver (FEKO / CST / HFSS) computes a target's RCS, the result is stored as a table over aspect and frequency, and that table is multiplied onto RAY-TRACED propagation paths.
negative_result_stated_carefully.how_hard: Five distinct query formulations across WebSearch, plus Crossref title resolution for every candidate that surfaced, plus targeted probes at ieeexplore, EuCAP/EuRAD proceedings, the ACM mobile-systems venues, and the Sionna-specific literature.
negative_result_stated_carefully.result: NOT FOUND. Every strong-venue instance located sources the table from a measurement campaign or from the authors' own asymptotic/ray solver, and the two commercial-solver instances known to us are LAMBDA (arXiv:2607.03826, preprint, ray-traced paths) and Rzewuski (NATO STO-MP-MSG-SET-183, published, but a link budget rather than ray-traced paths).
negative_result_stated_carefully.what_this_does_and_does_not_license: It licenses: 'we searched the strong venues for the commercial-solver-into-a-ray-tracer combination and did not find it.' It does NOT license: 'it has never been published.' Conference proceedings behind paywalls (EuCAP, EuRAD, GeMiC, ICMIM) are poorly indexed by general web search, and seven candidate items in this file are bibliographic-only. The honest statement is bounded by the method.

what_this_means_for_us: RETRACT the framing 'injection appears only in a preprint'. Injection has IEEE TAP (2008), IEEE TMTT (2022), IEEE TAES (2025), IEEE JSAC (2026), IET RSN (2020) and NATO STO behind it. The correct narrow claim is about ONE flavour: commercial-solver-RCS multiplied onto ray-traced paths is, as far as we have searched, still only a preprint.

Our architecture's nearest published relatives are Schuler (IEEE TAP 2008) and Deep (IET RSN 2020) - both compute the signature in their OWN ray/SBR solver, both validate it, both hand a reduced table to a downstream simulator. Cite these two as the architectural precedent, in that order.

The differentiator to prepare for review is ANCHORING, not architecture. Schuler validated against an anechoic bistatic campaign at the EC JRC before reducing; Potter's and Abadpour's tables ARE measurements. Our report13_sigma_grid needs its own independent anchor, and outputs/rcs_anchor.json (running now on GPU2) is precisely the artefact that discharges this obligation.

Zhao SCIS 2025 hands us a citable warning that applies directly to our own pipeline: monostatic-to-bistatic equivalence is 'reliable only for Bi-static angles less than 15-20 degrees'. Our chamber geometry needs to be checked against that number, and it connects to the standing 'RCS methodology' memo that our grid is monostatic-only.

The automotive generation-3 observation is the sharpest incoming criticism: modern asymptotic solvers do the scenario themselves, so injection there is a legacy pattern. Our defence has to be engine-specific - Sionna's stock PathSolver has no scattering integral - and must not be phrased as a general claim that injection is superior.

Table-BUILDING alone is publishable at a top venue. Two of the four new hits (Schuler TAP, Abadpour TMTT) produce a reusable signature table and state the downstream use as motivation without running it. That is a lower bar than we had assumed for report13's contribution.

method.tools: WebSearch and WebFetch for discovery; Crossref REST API (api.crossref.org) for authoritative venue / DOI / volume / pagination; Semantic Scholar Graph API for abstracts and open-access links; curl for PDF retrieval; PyMuPDF for text extraction and keyword-in-context grepping.
search_terms_combined: scattering center model + radar target simulator
what_was_NOT_done: No paywalled full texts were obtained. IEEE Xplore returned nothing to the fetcher; only open-access mirrors (KIT repository, arXiv, ETSI, MDPI/PMC) were read.

EuCAP, EuRAD, GeMiC and ICMIM proceedings were not searched inside their own indexes - only through general web search and Crossref title matching. This is the largest known blind spot and it sits exactly where the automotive injection line lives.
The ACM venues (MobiCom, SenSys, MobiSys, INFOCOM) were probed once each and produced no injection instance; that is a shallow pass, not a clean sweep.
The 10 instances in outputs/injection_archive.json were NOT re-verified here; they are cross-referenced, not re-derived.
No citation-graph traversal (forward citations of Schuler 2008 would very likely surface more consumers of the table, and was not run).
